name: Marpa Chökyi Lodrö (Marpa the Translator)
alt_names: mar pa chos kyi blo gros

realization_account.text: After years of study and gold-gathering journeys, Marpa received the complete transmissions from Nāropa; when Nāropa manifested Hevajra's maṇḍala Marpa prostrated to the deity rather than to his guru, and Nāropa foretold that his family line would scatter while his Dharma lineage would flourish through his disciples, like a river. He tested and trained Milarepa with harsh ordeals before giving him the instructions.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: Tibetan layman, farmer and translator of Lhodrak who travelled to India (three times by the usual account) and studied with Nāropa, Maitrīpa, Kukkuripa and others; he brought the Hevajra, Cakrasaṃvara, Guhyasamāja and Mahāmāyā tantras, the six dharmas and Mahāmudrā to Tibet and is the Tibetan founder of the Kagyu.
notes: His translations appear with Nāropa as co-translator in the colophons of Tōh 2304, 2330, 2337, 2338 (read locally). Drogmi's role as his first teacher is from the Life (moderate).

name: Dagmema
alt_names: bdag med ma (Tib., 'Nairātmyā', her name as Marpa's consort)

realization_account.text: She interceded for Milarepa and helped forge a letter so that Ngok Chöku Dorje would teach him; Marpa later said that without his permission the teaching could not bear fruit.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: Marpa's wife, remembered in the Life of Milarepa for her compassion toward Milarepa during his ordeals; in some accounts she dissolves into Marpa at death.

name: Darma Dode

realization_account.text: Knowing the transference into another body from his father, at death he transferred his consciousness into a pigeon and then into a brahmin boy's body in India (Tiphupa); after him the practice of grong 'jug is said to have ceased in Tibet.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: Marpa's son and intended heir, who died young after a fall from a horse; by the tradition's account he used the practice of 'entering another's body' (grong 'jug), first entering a dead pigeon that flew to India and then the corpse of a young brahmin, who became Tiphupa.
notes: The claim that transference into another body ended with him is the tradition's account (low).

name: Tiphupa

realization_account.text: Darma Dode's consciousness entered a pigeon, then a dead brahmin boy's body; the boy revived and became the yogin Tiphupa ('the pigeon one').
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: Indian yogin who, by the Kagyu account, was the rebirth (through transference) of Marpa's son Darma Dode; he taught Rechungpa in India.

name: Ngok Chöku Dorje

realization_account.text: Received from Marpa the explanation (bshad pa) of the tantras; Milarepa came to him with the forged letter.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: One of Marpa's four principal disciples ('the four pillars'), holder of the explanatory lineage of the tantras (especially Hevajra); founder of the Ngok tradition of the Marpa Kagyu.

name: Tsurtön Wangi Dorje
alt_names: mtshur ston dbang gi rdo rje
summary: One of Marpa's four principal disciples, holder of the Guhyasamāja transmission and (by one account) of transference.

name: Meton Chenpo (Meton Tsönpo)
summary: One of Marpa's four principal disciples, holder (by one account) of the clear-light instruction.
notes: The allotment 'Ngok — explanation, Tsur — transference, Meton — clear light, Mila — inner heat' is from memory of the Kagyu histories (low).

name: Milarepa (Jetsün Mila Shepa Dorje)
alt_names: Mila Shepa Dorje (mi la bzhad pa rdo rje)

realization_account.text: Having killed thirty-five people through sorcery and destroyed crops with hail, he felt remorse, sought Dharma, and was made by Marpa to build and tear down towers until his evil karma was purified; after empowerment he meditated alone for years, living on nettles until his body turned green; he attained realization through inner heat and Mahāmudrā, displayed miraculous powers (flight; the contest with Naro Bönchung at Kailash), and at death, poisoned by a jealous scholar, showed signs of buddhahood.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: The great yogin-poet of Tibet: after using sorcery to avenge his family he turned to the Dharma, endured Marpa's ordeals, practised for years in mountain caves wearing only cotton cloth (repa) and sustained by inner heat, and attained buddhahood in one life by the tradition's account; teacher of Gampopa and Rechungpa; his songs are the Hundred Thousand Songs.
notes: Details of the life are from Tsangnyön Heruka's 1488 version; earlier lives differ in details.

name: Lama Yungtön Trogyal
summary: The sorcerer (a Nyingma mantrin) from whom, in the Life of Milarepa, the young Milarepa learned the destructive magic he used against his relatives.

name: Rongtön Lhaga

realization_account.text: He told Milarepa that his Dzogchen was such that one who meditates on it by day is awakened by day; Milarepa, overconfident, did not practise and gained nothing, and was sent to Marpa, with whom he had a karmic link.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: The Dzogchen teacher who, in the Life of Milarepa, gave Milarepa the Great Perfection before sending him to Marpa, because Milarepa's karma did not suit it.

name: Rechungpa Dorje Drakpa
alt_names: ras chung pa rdo rje grags pa

realization_account.text: Proud of the learning he brought from India, he was humbled by Milarepa's display (sheltering inside a yak horn); Milarepa's Life is framed as told to him.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: Milarepa's close disciple, called his 'moon-like' son (Gampopa being the 'sun-like'); he went to India and brought back from Tiphupa the teachings of the formless ḍākinīs; source of the Rechung hearing lineage and, by the Drukpa account, of the Six Equal Tastes hidden as treasure.

name: Peta Gönkyi
summary: Milarepa's sister, who after long hardship became his disciple and a practitioner.

name: Paldarbum
summary: A woman disciple of Milarepa to whom, in the Hundred Thousand Songs, he sings a famous song on meditation using the images of sky, sun and moon, mountain, ocean and mind.

name: Seben Repa
summary: A cotton-clad disciple of Milarepa named in the Hundred Thousand Songs.

name: Ngendzong Repa
summary: A disciple of Milarepa associated with an early collection of his songs and teachings (the Ngendzong hearing lineage).

name: Gampopa Sönam Rinchen (Dakpo Lhaje)
alt_names: sgam po pa bsod nams rin chen
Candraprabhakumāra (identified by the tradition with the bodhisattva of the Samādhirāja Sūtra)

realization_account.text: Foretold in the Samādhirāja Sūtra (by the tradition's reading) as a physician-monk who would spread its teaching; he came to Milarepa already accomplished in Kadam meditation, reported his experiences, and was told they were neither good nor bad; Milarepa's parting instruction was to show his calloused seat from years of sitting.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: Physician of Dakpo who, after his wife's death, became a Kadampa monk and then Milarepa's chief disciple; he joined the Kadam graded path with Milarepa's Mahāmudrā and Six Yogas, founded Daklha Gampo (1121) and wrote the Jewel Ornament of Liberation; all the Dakpo Kagyu schools descend from his disciples.
notes: His Kadam teachers (e.g. Geshe Nyukrumpa, Jayulwa) are not given ids here.

name: Dakpo Gomtsul Tsultrim Nyingpo
summary: Gampopa's nephew and successor at Daklha Gampo; teacher of Lama Zhang.

name: Düsum Khyenpa, the first Karmapa
alt_names: dus gsum mkhyen pa ('knower of the three times')

realization_account.text: He attained realization at fifty; the ḍākinīs are said to have woven a crown from their hair and offered it to him — the origin of the Karmapa's black crown.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: Disciple of Gampopa (after studying Madhyamaka and logic with Kadam teachers), founder of the Karma Kagyu and of the monasteries of Kampo Nenang, Karma Gön and Tsurphu; regarded as the first Karmapa.

name: Phagmodrupa Dorje Gyalpo
alt_names: phag mo gru pa rdo rje rgyal po
summary: Disciple of Gampopa (and before him of Sachen Kunga Nyingpo in the Lamdre), founder of Densa Thil; eight of his disciples founded the 'eight lesser' Kagyu schools.

name: Barom Darma Wangchuk
summary: Disciple of Gampopa, founder of the Barom Kagyu.

name: Lama Zhang (Zhang Yudrakpa Tsöndrü Drakpa)
alt_names: zhang g.yu brag pa brtson 'grus grags pa
summary: Founder of the Tsalpa Kagyu and of Tshal Gungthang; disciple of Gomtsul; author of the Ultimate Supreme Path of Mahāmudrā; also a political figure in the Lhasa region.

name: Jigten Sumgön (Drikung Kyobpa Rinchen Pal)
alt_names: 'bri gung skyob pa rin chen dpal
summary: Disciple of Phagmodrupa, founder of the Drikung Kagyu at Drikung Thil (1179); teacher of the 'single intent' and the fivefold Mahāmudrā; sent large numbers of retreatants to Kailash, Lapchi and Tsari.

name: Sherab Jungne
summary: Disciple of Jigten Sumgön who compiled his vajra statements as the Gongchig ('Single Intent').

name: Rigdzin Chökyi Drakpa
summary: Drikung master and treasure revealer (16th–17th c.) who joined Drikung Mahāmudrā with Dzogchen (the Drikung Yangzab).

name: Taklung Thangpa Tashi Pal
alt_names: stag lung thang pa bkra shis dpal
summary: Disciple of Phagmodrupa, founder of Taklung monastery (1180) and of the Taklung Kagyu.

name: Gyaltsa Rinchen Gön
summary: Disciple of Phagmodrupa associated with the founding of the Trophu Kagyu (with Kunden Repa).

name: Martsang Sherab Senge (Marpa Drubthob)
summary: Disciple of Phagmodrupa, founder of the Martsang Kagyu.

name: Yelpa Yeshe Tsek
summary: Disciple of Phagmodrupa, founder of the Yelpa Kagyu.

name: Zarawa Kalden Yeshe Senge
summary: Disciple of Phagmodrupa associated with the founding of the Yazang Kagyu.

name: Gyergom Tsultrim Senge
summary: Disciple of Phagmodrupa, founder of the Shugseb Kagyu.

name: Lingje Repa Pema Dorje
alt_names: gling rje ras pa padma rdo rje
summary: Disciple of Phagmodrupa, a wandering yogin-poet and the teacher of Tsangpa Gyare; forerunner of the Drukpa.

name: Tsangpa Gyare Yeshe Dorje (the first Gyalwang Drukpa)
alt_names: gtsang pa rgya ras ye shes rdo rje

realization_account.text: At Namdruk he heard thunder and saw nine dragons rise into the sky, and named his lineage Drukpa, 'of the Dragon'.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: Founder of the Drukpa Kagyu at Ralung (1180) and Druk (1189); disciple of Lingje Repa; rediscoverer (by the tradition's account) of the Six Equal Tastes hidden by Rechungpa; the first of the Gyalwang Drukpa incarnations.

name: Gyalwa Götsangpa Gönpo Dorje
alt_names: rgod tshang pa mgon po rdo rje
summary: Disciple of Tsangpa Gyare, founder of the Upper Drukpa and exemplar of the mountain-retreat life; teacher of Orgyenpa and Yangönpa.

name: Gyalwa Lorepa Wangchuk Tsöndrü
alt_names: lo ras pa dbang phyug brtson 'grus
summary: Disciple of Tsangpa Gyare, founder of the Lower Drukpa, known for strict renunciate discipline.

name: Yangönpa Gyaltsen Pal
alt_names: yang dgon pa rgyal mtshan dpal
summary: Drukpa master, disciple of Götsangpa, author of the Hidden Description of the Vajra Body and of mountain-retreat teachings.

name: Orgyenpa Rinchen Pal
alt_names: o rgyan pa rin chen dpal
summary: Drukpa master, disciple of Götsangpa, famous for his journey to Oḍḍiyāna and the 'approach and accomplishment of the three vajras' received there; teacher of the 3rd Karmapa, whom (by the tradition's account) he recognized as the rebirth of Karma Pakshi.

name: Pema Karpo (the fourth Gyalwang Drukpa)
summary: The great scholar of the Drukpa: author of works on Mahāmudrā, the Six Yogas, history, grammar and medicine, who systematized Drukpa practice and defended the Kagyu Mahāmudrā.
notes: The dispute over his rebirth (Paksam Wangpo vs Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal) led to the Zhabdrung's flight to Bhutan (1616).

name: Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal
alt_names: zhabs drung ngag dbang rnam rgyal
summary: Drukpa hierarch recognized by one party as Pema Karpo's rebirth; after the succession dispute he went to Bhutan (1616), unified it, and founded the Southern Drukpa state tradition.

name: Drukpa Kunley (Kunga Legpa)
summary: The Drukpa 'divine madman' of Tibet and Bhutan, whose satirical songs and outrageous conduct are remembered as teaching.

name: Tsangnyön Heruka Sangye Gyaltsen
alt_names: gtsang smyon he ru ka sangs rgyas rgyal mtshan
summary: The 'madman of Tsang', a Kagyu yogin who compiled and printed the Life and the Hundred Thousand Songs of Milarepa (1488) and the Life of Marpa.

name: Lhatsün Rinchen Namgyal
alt_names: lha btsun rin chen rnam rgyal
summary: Disciple of Tsangnyön Heruka, author of a Life of Nāropa and editor of Kagyu texts.

name: Karma Pakshi, the second Karmapa
summary: Master of the Mongol courts (Möngke Khan; later persecuted under Kublai); by the tradition's account the first recognized reincarnation (tulku) in Tibet, the rebirth of Düsum Khyenpa.

name: Rangjung Dorje, the third Karmapa
summary: Scholar-yogin who synthesized Mahāmudrā, the Six Yogas and Dzogchen (the Karma Nyingthig); author of the Profound Inner Meaning, the Aspiration Prayer of Mahāmudrā, Distinguishing Consciousness and Wisdom and the Treatise on Buddha-Nature; recognized as a child by Orgyenpa.

name: Rolpe Dorje, the fourth Karmapa
summary: Poet and teacher at the Yuan court; by the tradition's account he gave lay vows to the child Tsongkhapa.

name: Deshin Shekpa, the fifth Karmapa
summary: Invited by the Yongle emperor to Nanjing (1407); by the tradition's account the emperor, seeing the ḍākinī-woven crown above the Karmapa's head, had a material replica made — the black crown of the ceremony.

name: Thongwa Dönden, the sixth Karmapa
summary: Karmapa who compiled Kagyu liturgies and rituals.

name: Chödrak Gyatso, the seventh Karmapa
summary: Scholar Karmapa, author on pramāṇa (the Ocean of Texts on Reasoning).

name: Mikyö Dorje, the eighth Karmapa
summary: The great scholar Karmapa: author of the Chariot of the Dakpo Kagyu Siddhas (Madhyamaka), the Four-Session Guru Yoga, and compiler of the Kagyu Gurtso; defended the Kagyu view against Gelug critics.

name: Wangchuk Dorje, the ninth Karmapa
summary: Author of the three classic Karma Kagyu Mahāmudrā manuals: the Ocean of Definitive Meaning, Dispelling the Darkness of Ignorance and Pointing Out the Dharmakāya.

name: Chöying Dorje, the tenth Karmapa
summary: Painter and sculptor Karmapa who lived years in exile during the wars of the 1640s that brought the Fifth Dalai Lama's government to power.

name: Yeshe Dorje, the eleventh Karmapa
summary: Short-lived Karmapa who also held Nyingma treasure teachings.

name: Changchub Dorje, the twelfth Karmapa
summary: Karmapa who travelled with the 8th Situ to Nepal and China and died young.

name: Düdul Dorje, the thirteenth Karmapa
summary: Karmapa remembered for his affinity with animals.

name: Thekchok Dorje, the fourteenth Karmapa
summary: Karmapa of the Rimé era, teacher and student of Jamgön Kongtrul and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

name: Khakhyab Dorje, the fifteenth Karmapa
summary: Scholar Karmapa, disciple of Jamgön Kongtrul.

name: Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, the sixteenth Karmapa
alt_names: rang byung rig pa'i rdo rje
summary: Karmapa who left Tibet in 1959, founded Rumtek in Sikkim and spread the Karma Kagyu internationally.

name: Ogyen Trinley Dorje (recognized as seventeenth Karmapa by one party)
summary: One of two claimants recognized as the seventeenth Karmapa (recognized by the Tai Situpa and endorsed by the Dalai Lama); left Tibet in 2000.

name: Trinley Thaye Dorje (recognized as seventeenth Karmapa by one party)
summary: One of two claimants recognized as the seventeenth Karmapa (recognized by the Shamarpa).

name: Pomdrakpa Sönam Dorje
alt_names: spom brag pa bsod nams rdo rje
summary: Karma Kagyu master, disciple of Drogön Rechen (himself a disciple of Düsum Khyenpa) and teacher of Karma Pakshi, through whom the first Karmapa's transmission reached the second.
notes: Low confidence on the name form, dates and relationship.

name: Khedrup Drakpa Senge, the first Shamarpa
alt_names: mkhas grub grags pa seng ge
summary: Disciple of the 3rd Karmapa, first of the Shamarpa ('red crown') incarnations of the Karma Kagyu.

name: Situ Paṇchen Chökyi Jungne (the eighth Tai Situpa)
alt_names: si tu paN chen chos kyi 'byung gnas
summary: Scholar of grammar, medicine and art, editor of the Derge Kangyur (1733), founder of Palpung; revived the Karma Kagyu and favoured the shentong reading.

name: Pawo Tsuglag Trengwa (the second Pawo)
alt_names: dpa' bo gtsug lag phreng ba
summary: Karma Kagyu historian, author of A Feast for Scholars.

name: Karma Trinlepa
summary: Karma Kagyu scholar, teacher of the 8th Karmapa, commentator on the songs of the Kagyu masters.

name: Gö Lotsāwa Zhönu Pal
alt_names: 'gos lo tsA ba gzhon nu dpal
summary: Translator and historian, author of the Blue Annals and of a commentary on the Ratnagotravibhāga that presents it as a basis of Mahāmudrā; affiliated with the Karma Kagyu and others.

name: Dakpo Tashi Namgyal
alt_names: dwags po bkra shis rnam rgyal
summary: Abbot of Daklha Gampo, scholar of the Dakpo Kagyu, author of Moonbeams of Mahāmudrā and of works on the Six Yogas and on tantra.

name: Tselé Natsok Rangdröl
alt_names: rtse le sna tshogs rang grol
summary: Kagyu and Nyingma master of the 17th c., author of the Lamp of Mahāmudrā and of works joining Mahāmudrā and Dzogchen.

name: Bengar Jampal Zangpo
summary: Karma Kagyu yogin (15th c.), author of the Dorje Chang Thungma lineage prayer; teacher of the 7th Karmapa by the usual account.

name: Chögyam Trungpa
summary: Holder of the Surmang Kagyu and Nyingma lineages who taught in the West (from 1970) and founded Shambhala; recent.

name: Khyungpo Naljor
alt_names: khyung po rnal 'byor tshul khrims mgon po

tradition.text: 978/990–1127/1139 (a life of about 150 years in the tradition's reckoning)

scholarly.text: 11th–12th c.; the traditional life-span is not accepted by modern historians

realization_account.text: He met Niguma in a charnel ground (Sosaling), where she appeared in the sky as a dark-skinned ḍākinī; she taught him in dreams and waking, and bade that the teachings pass to one disciple at a time for seven generations.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: Tibetan yogin, first trained in Bön and Dzogchen, who travelled to India and Nepal, received the six dharmas and the Amulet Mahāmudrā from Niguma and teachings from Sukhasiddhi, Maitrīpa and others, and founded the Shangpa Kagyu with its seat at Zhong-zhong in Shang.

name: Mokchokpa Rinchen Tsöndrü
alt_names: rmog lcog pa rin chen brtson 'grus
summary: Second of the Shangpa 'seven jewels', disciple of Khyungpo Naljor.

name: Kyergangpa Chökyi Senge
alt_names: skyer sgang pa chos kyi seng ge
summary: Third of the Shangpa 'seven jewels', disciple of Mokchokpa.

name: Rigongpa Sangye Nyentön
alt_names: ri gong pa sangs rgyas gnyan ston
summary: Fourth of the Shangpa 'seven jewels'.

name: Sangye Tönpa Tsöndrü Senge
alt_names: sangs rgyas ston pa brtson 'grus seng ge
summary: Fifth of the Shangpa 'seven jewels' (counting Vajradhara and Niguma), after whom the Shangpa spread through several disciples.
notes: The counting of the 'seven jewels' (Vajradhara, Niguma, Khyungpo Naljor, Mokchokpa, Kyergangpa, Nyentön, Sangye Tönpa) is from memory.

name: Thangtong Gyalpo

scholarly.text: 14th–15th c.; the long life-span is the tradition's

summary: Yogin, engineer and holder of the Shangpa (and of a Niguma lineage received by vision), famous for building iron-chain bridges, for founding Tibetan opera by tradition, and for the Avalokiteśvara practice 'Benefit of Beings Pervading Space'.
